title: Bates Numbering
description: Assign each produced document a Bates range with a `for...of` carrying a running counter — algorithm shape, because each doc's range depends on the cumulative page count of everything before it.

notes: `padStart(width, '0')` produces fixed-width labels (EVE000001) so the strings sort and collate in numeric order — essential when documents are produced and referenced by Bates number.
The `next` counter carries state across iterations, so this is a `for...of`, not a pure `.map`: each doc's range depends on the cumulative page count of all prior docs.
Off-by-one: `end = next + pages - 1`. A 2-page doc starting at 1 spans 1..2 (not 1..3), and the next doc starts at `end + 1`.

options: Fixed-width zero-padded labels sort and collate in numeric order as strings — EVE000002 < EVE000010, which 'EVE2' vs 'EVE10' would get wrong
Bates numbers are required to be exactly 6 digits by law
questions.explain: String sort is lexicographic: 'EVE10' sorts before 'EVE2'. Zero-padding to a fixed width makes lexicographic order match numeric order, which is what document-production tooling relies on.

questions.q: Why is this a `for...of` with a `next` variable rather than `docs.map(d => ...)`?
options: Each doc's Bates range depends on the running page count of all prior docs — the iteration carries state that isn't a clean per-element transform
`for...of` is faster on arrays of objects
questions.explain: The start number for doc N is determined by how many pages docs 0..N-1 consumed. That cross-element accumulation is algorithm-shape; a `.map` would need to mutate an external counter, which is the anti-pattern.

questions.q: A document starts at Bates 4 and has 5 pages. What is its `end`, computed as `next + pages - 1`?
questions.explain: Pages 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 — that's 5 pages ending at 8. `4 + 5 - 1 = 8`. Forgetting the `- 1` would claim the doc occupies page 9 too and shift every subsequent doc.

questions.q: Why does the code special-case `d.pages === 1` to emit a single label instead of a range?
options: A range with equal start and end (EVE000003-EVE000003) is redundant and not how single-page docs are cited
It is purely a performance optimization
questions.explain: A one-page document is cited by a single Bates number, not a degenerate range like EVE000003-EVE000003. The conditional keeps the output matching real legal-production convention.

exercises.prompt: Build a fixed-width Bates label. Fill the blanks so a page number renders as a 6-digit zero-padded string with the EVE prefix.

blanks.hint: pad on the left so the total width is fixed

exercises.prompt: Advance a running Bates counter across two docs. Fill the blanks so the second doc's start is logged.

blanks.hint: the counter after advancing past doc 1

L3.prompt: Assign each produced document a Bates range: prefix `EVE`, 6-digit zero-padded, starting at 1. A 1-page doc gets a single label; multi-page gets `start-end`.
L3.expectedOutput:
Intake: EVE000001-EVE000002
X-Ray: EVE000003
ER Report: EVE000004-EVE000008
hints: Keep a `let next = 1` counter outside the loop; for each doc `start = next`, `end = next + d.pages - 1`, then `next = end + 1`.
